svg.text: Ladder diagram (LD, IEC 61131-3) – 5 basic patterns with the HMC01 tags of this guide
Left rail = +24 V idea, current flows left to right. -| |- NO contact (TRUE when bit = 1), -|/|- NC contact (TRUE when bit = 0), -( )- coil.
ISO 13850: after E-stop only a NEW start edge sets RunEnable
The seal-in contact is in parallel ONLY to the start
button. Any series contact that opens drops RunEnable.
Network 2 – mutual interlock lift up / down (APC)
two valves must never be ON together
Machine-protection interlock in the standard PLC.
Person protection is in the F-program (chapter 28).
APC addresses from guide 09 (own address block).
Network 3 – on-delay timer TON – debounce part sensor 100 ms
Q = 1 when IN has been 1 for PT
TON: Q follows IN after PT; IN = 0 resets ET at once.
TOF: Q stays 1 for PT after IN goes 0. TP: pulse of PT.
Max PT in a 32-bit TIME = T#24D20H31M23S647MS (24.8 days).
Network 4 – up counter CTU – tool life (0.45 % wear per part → 222 parts)
P contact = rising edge: one count per cycle,
not one count per scan. Use DINT for production
32767 × 345 s = 130.8 days at one part per cycle.
Network 5 – alarm latch with set / reset coils (S) (R)
limit 75 °C, reset only when value < 73 °C AND operator acknowledged
S/R coils keep their state between scans – write
each S/R pair in ONE place only (one writer rule).
seal-in, interlock, timer TON, counter CTU, set/reset – HMC01 tags
